bull_bear.body: Focus on fit-out capital for high-pre-lease assets; No heavy land acquisition; Reinvesting operating cash flows into rapid Tier-2 expansion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on massive 8 lakh sq. ft. delivery; Concentration in Gujarat/Rajasthan; Potential slowdown in GCC hiring; Competition from institutional players entering Tier-2.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, strategic pivot emphasized, focused on 'virtual entry barriers' in Tier-2, proud of asset-light innovation.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 8 lakh sq. ft. deal is a 'Development Management' contract where DevX acts as the operator/consultant for non-institutional landowners, effectively institutionalizing fragmented Tier-2 supply without balance sheet burden.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet deleveraged: Net Debt / (Cash) fell from Rs. 127 Cr in FY25 to Rs. 89 Cr in FY26 and Rs. 81 Cr in Q1 FY27; gross debt was Rs. 135 Cr against Rs. 54 Cr of cash in Q1 FY27.
- Leverage ratios improved sharply - Gross Debt/Equity 2.39x (FY25) to 0.66x (Q1 FY27), Net Debt/Equity 2.32x to 0.40x, and Net Debt/EBITDA (IGAAP) 5.90x to 1.04x; credit rating is ACUITE BBB Stable Outlook on long term borrowings.
- "We have also raised Rs. 100 crore through non-convertible debt, further diversifying our sources of capital and providing additional resources to support our planned expansion."
- Promoter alignment: "upon conversion of the recently issued preferential warrants, the promoter shareholding is expected to increase from the current 36.81% to approximately 37.29%".
- Returns profile improving on the deck's own historical series: ROCE 5.0% (FY24), 12.0% (FY25), 14.0% (FY26) and ROE 3.6%, 4.3%, 7.4% over the same years.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- customer lock-in: long-tenure managed-office contracts with 5-9 year lease terms and 3.5-5 year lock-ins — evidence: zero net churn and 99.7% seat-retention rate in FY 2025-26
- scale: largest managed workspace operator in India's Tier II markets by operational flex stock — evidence: 28 operational centres across 12 cities with 13,604+ seating capacity
- cost position: asset-light straight-lease model bearing only fit-out costs while retaining full revenue upside — evidence: debt-to-equity improved to 0.78x in FY 2025-26 from 2.39x in FY 2024-25 following IPO proceeds
- integration: in-house design-and-build capability removes the largest source of delay in client expansion — evidence: bespoke workspace delivered within 75-90 days via subsidiary Neddle and Thread Designs LLP
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Lease-Commitment Mismatch — Long landlord leases (5-9 years) against flexible client contracts create a lease-commitment mismatch; fixed rental obligations persist even if occupancy softens.
- Client Concentration — A significant share of revenue is derived from the top 20 clients; the loss or non-renewal of a major occupier could affect revenue.
- Technology/AI Demand Shift — AI and automation may moderate headcount growth among IT/ITeS and GCC occupiers, softening seat demand, even as higher-value GCC mandates expand.
- Supply Chain and Labour — Material-cost volatility and labour shortages may increase fit-out costs and delay centre deliveries, affecting expansion timelines and margins.
- Competition and Pricing — A fragmented market with many operators and price competition in some submarkets can pressure occupancy, rentals and margins.
- Execution and Expansion — Expansion and the early-stage development-management model carry execution and capital-commitment risk if new centres underperform or projects face delays.
- Geopolitical and Macroeconomic — A sharp slowdown or sustained energy-price shock would weigh on occupier hiring and expansion, reducing demand for workspace; the risk remains largely external and uncontrollable.
- Geographic Concentration — A significant portion of the Company's revenue is derived from Ahmedabad.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Managed Workspace: 75% revenue from Tier-2, 88.4% occupancy, 98% retention; Design & Build: INR 38.8 Cr (9M), 16.8% margin, 19+ projects delivered; Tech/Payroll: Cross-sell via SaaSjoy to increase wallet share.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for cost-arbitrage and scalable Grade-A infrastructure outside saturated metros | Global Capability Centers (GCCs) | beneficiary | High | DevX provides end-to-end solution (real estate + hiring + tech) in Tier-2 cities where GCCs are migrating for 20-35% cost savings. |
| Fragmented, non-institutional land ownership in Tier-2 cities lacking enterprise-grade assets | Tier-2 Landowners | beneficiary | Med | DevX partners with them to develop Grade-A assets and manages leasing, unlocking value from idle land. |
| High rental costs and saturation in Tier-1 markets | Traditional Tier-1 Co-working Operators | loser | Med | DevX's aggressive Tier-2 focus and asset-light model create a 'virtual entry barrier' making it hard for metro-centric players to compete on cost/scale in emerging cities. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Our Platform Connects Landlords, Clients and Vendor Partners - Creating a Powerful Network Effect for All": non-institutional landlords get a "One stop solution with guaranteed results", enterprise clients get "Flexible, efficient offices in just 75-90 days", and vendor partners get "Access to assured footfalls and projects".
- Presence of 27 centers across 12 Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities and 6 states; Tier 1 accounts for 20% of SBA (10 centers), Tier 2 Gujarat 73% (13 centers) and Tier 2 other states 7% (4 centers). Revenue split by tier is 74% Tier 2 / 26% Tier 1 and by state 66% Gujarat.
- Enterprise clients are the core: Enterprise Client % of Revenue from Operations rose to 70% in Q1 FY27 from 52% in Q1 FY26; the Chairman notes "increasing demand for highly customised and technology-enabled workspaces".
- "Single Delivery Platform for GCC" spanning Managed Office Space + Development Management (80% of Q1 FY27 revenue), Design & Build (18%) and GCC (2%), where "Design and technology capabilities accelerate client acquisition, deepen retention and maximize occupancy".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [AI Launchpad] The company is developing "a technology-led real estate ecosystem through the AI Infrastructure Launchpad, which invites AI and PropTech innovators to develop solutions aimed at improving operational efficiency, automating processes, enhancing customer experience and enabling data-driven decision-making".
- [Tokenisation] "Tokenization process has been started, law firm and related consultants on boarded and entity incorporation started"; the Chairman adds that "Recent building tokenisation initiatives and access to global capital are expected to support expansion plans in this area".
- [Investment - Eezily] DevX is "leveraging its investment in Eezily to gain access to broker networks, real estate market intelligence and demand insights, creating synergies between AI, data and its operating platform".
- [Partnership] "The partnership with a leading pan-India media organisation will also provide access to a wider innovation network and help identify scalable technology solutions." (the counterparty is not named in the deck)
- [OpCo-PropCo] The company "Commenced operations as the lessee of the JUPL/AEPL property and will continue to manage the office space under the OpCo-PropCo model", which "Separates operational management from property ownership, enabling scalable and efficient operations".
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: DevX operates an integrated workspace platform spanning design, fit-outs, management and allied services, sourcing bare-shell properties and transforming them into fully managed, technology-enabled campuses for enterprises, MNCs and GCCs. Its ecosystem comprises DevX Spaces (managed workspace under built-to-suit contracts), DevX D&B (in-house design-and-build via subsidiary Neddle and Thread Designs LLP) and DevX GCC (software, cloud and allied technology services via subsidiary Saasjoy Solutions Private Limited, supporting Global Capability Centres). The company primarily focuses on Tier-II and emerging commercial markets, serving medium and large enterprises with requirements exceeding 300 seats.

- **DevX D&B:** Design-and-build services (Neddle and Thread Designs LLP)

- **Coworking:** Coworking space

latest_quarter.body: Rent-to-Revenue ratio improved to 2.62x (Tier-2) vs 2.1x (Tier-1); Rental escalations 4-5% (cost) vs 5-6% (revenue); Large centers benefit from 8-12 months rent-free periods and lower common area % (16% vs 22-25%).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Targeting ~INR 350 Cr for FY27; Margin: New large centers to operate at 60-65% margin initially (rent-free), stabilizing at 30-45%; Order Inflow: Strong pipeline in Lucknow, Bhubaneswar, Coimbatore, Kochi; Capex: Shift to development management model reduces own capex to fit-outs only.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 8.15 lakh sq. ft. (Ahmedabad Ambli-Bopal, signed Q3, 4-year rollout); 3.15 lakh sq. ft. (Ahmedabad Capital One, 95% pre-leased, operational Feb/Mar 2026); 4 new centers in pipeline (Pune, Million Minds Ahmedabad, GMDC Ahmedabad).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Replicating the 8 lakh sq. ft. development management template in other Tier-2 cities; Expanding into 4 new cities (Lucknow, Bhubaneswar, Coimbatore, Kochi); Capturing 20%+ GCC migration to Tier-2.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Corridor-led, Tier-II focused expansion strategy prioritising enterprise demand over asset ownership
- Asset-light Development Management model: partnering with landowners to create purpose-built, institutional-grade supply based on confirmed enterprise demand rather than leasing ready-made space
- Enterprise-first business design targeting long-term workspace requirements over short-duration coworking demand
- Direct-first client sourcing (reducing reliance on channel partners) to lower acquisition costs and strengthen enterprise engagement
- Integrated platform combining development management, workplace operations and technology (DevX Terra) on a single platform
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: DevX's next phase of growth targets expanding operational portfolio from approximately 8.3 Lacs Sq. Ft. to 12 Lacs Sq. Ft. by FY 2027-28, funded via a diversified capital strategy including Non-Convertible Debentures of `100 Crores (indicative coupon 11.75%, listed on BSE Debt Segment) and a preferential issue. Key near-term projects: DevX 052 in Ahmedabad — India's largest single managed office mandate, an 8.60 Lacs Sq. Ft. contract adding ~8,500 seats, expected to generate approximately `120 Crores in annual revenue upon stabilisation, supported by a planned investment of `100 Crores over four years. DevX Capital One, Ahmedabad — 3.15 Lacs Sq. Ft. now operational, achieved nearly 95% pre-leasing before commencement, contributing `2.65-2.75 Crores monthly. DevX Million Minds, Ahmedabad — 84,000 Sq. Ft. operational. DevX LakeShore & DevX Featherlite at Outer Ring Road, Bengaluru (Prestige) — 1.1 Lacs Sq. Ft., operational from August 2026, establishing a presence in a premier Bengaluru commercial corridor. Pune expansion — 42,000 Sq. Ft. followed by 2,04,000 Sq. Ft. scheduled for January 2027. DevX 102, Ahmedabad Development Management — 5 Lacs Sq. Ft. targeted to go live in Q4 FY 2026-27, demonstrating scalability of the Development Management model. The company also operates a Development Management model in Ahmedabad's Ambli-Bopal corridor, with approximately 8.60 Lacs Sq. Ft. contracted, generating development management fees of `300-500 per Sq. Ft. in addition to recurring managed-workspace revenues.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Enterprise clients contributed 65% of FY 2025-26 revenue, supported by longer lease tenures, deeper client relationships and greater visibility of future occupancy
- Approximately 78% of seats during FY 2025-26 were sourced directly rather than through channel partners, reducing acquisition costs
- Brokerage costs as a percentage of revenue declined from 1.70% in FY 2023-24 to 1.47% in FY 2024-25 and 1.39% in FY 2025-26, reflecting a strengthening enterprise franchise
- Close to three-fourths of FY 2025-26 revenue originated from Tier-II markets, validating the corridor-led expansion strategy
- Seat retention rate of 99.7% and zero net churn, supported by average client relationships of approximately 3.5 years and contractual lock-ins averaging 2.5 years
- Signed Pipeline of 23.68 Lacs Sq. Ft. across 10 centres and 32,739 seats, alongside 5.04 Lacs Sq. Ft. under fit-out across 4 centres and 7,137 seats
- Manubhai and Shah LLP: a client for over six years, with ~2,609 seats across 6 centres and `133 Crores in contracted total revenue
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: DevX cemented its Tier-2 moat by signing a landmark 8.15 lakh sq. ft. development management deal in Ahmedabad, shifting capex burden to landowners while securing 95% pre-leasing on a 3.15 lakh sq. ft. campus. This structural pivot, combined with 53% YoY revenue growth and 46% EBITDA margins, validates the 'asset-light operator' model for Global Capability Centers (GCCs) outside metros.

risks.note: Long landlord leases (5-9 years) against flexible client contracts create a lease-commitment mismatch; fixed rental obligations persist even if occupancy softens.
A significant share of revenue is derived from the top 20 clients; the loss or non-renewal of a major occupier could affect revenue.
AI and automation may moderate headcount growth among IT/ITeS and GCC occupiers, softening seat demand, even as higher-value GCC mandates expand.
Material-cost volatility and labour shortages may increase fit-out costs and delay centre deliveries, affecting expansion timelines and margins.
A fragmented market with many operators and price competition in some submarkets can pressure occupancy, rentals and margins.
Expansion and the early-stage development-management model carry execution and capital-commitment risk if new centres underperform or projects face delays.
A sharp slowdown or sustained energy-price shock would weigh on occupier hiring and expansion, reducing demand for workspace; the risk remains largely external and uncontrollable.
A significant portion of the Company's revenue is derived from Ahmedabad.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: DevX is the largest managed workspace operator in India's Tier II markets in terms of operational flex stock, providing fully managed, technology-enabled office solutions to enterprises, MNCs and GCCs on a zero-capex-to-client model.

business_model.body: DevX operates an integrated workspace platform spanning design, fit-outs, management and allied services, sourcing bare-shell properties and transforming them into fully managed, technology-enabled campuses for enterprises, MNCs and GCCs. Its ecosystem comprises DevX Spaces (managed workspace under built-to-suit contracts), DevX D&B (in-house design-and-build via subsidiary Neddle and Thread Designs LLP) and DevX GCC (software, cloud and allied technology services via subsidiary Saasjoy Solutions Private Limited, supporting Global Capability Centres). The company primarily focuses on Tier-II and emerging commercial markets, serving medium and large enterprises with requirements exceeding 300 seats.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Targeting ~INR 350 Cr for FY27; Margin: New large centers to operate at 60-65% margin initially (rent-free), stabilizing at 30-45%; Order Inflow: Strong pipeline in Lucknow, Bhubaneswar, Coimbatore, Kochi; Capex: Shift to development management model reduces own capex to fit-outs only.

growth_optionality.body: Replicating the 8 lakh sq. ft. development management template in other Tier-2 cities; Expanding into 4 new cities (Lucknow, Bhubaneswar, Coimbatore, Kochi); Capturing 20%+ GCC migration to Tier-2.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Enterprise clients contributed 65% of FY 2025-26 revenue, supported by longer lease tenures, deeper client relationships and greater visibility of future occupancy
- Approximately 78% of seats during FY 2025-26 were sourced directly rather than through channel partners, reducing acquisition costs
- Brokerage costs as a percentage of revenue declined from 1.70% in FY 2023-24 to 1.47% in FY 2024-25 and 1.39% in FY 2025-26, reflecting a strengthening enterprise franchise
- Close to three-fourths of FY 2025-26 revenue originated from Tier-II markets, validating the corridor-led expansion strategy
- Seat retention rate of 99.7% and zero net churn, supported by average client relationships of approximately 3.5 years and contractual lock-ins averaging 2.5 years
- Signed Pipeline of 23.68 Lacs Sq. Ft. across 10 centres and 32,739 seats, alongside 5.04 Lacs Sq. Ft. under fit-out across 4 centres and 7,137 seats
- Manubhai and Shah LLP: a client for over six years, with ~2,609 seats across 6 centres and `133 Crores in contracted total revenue

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Rent-to-Revenue ratio improved to 2.62x (Tier-2) vs 2.1x (Tier-1); Rental escalations 4-5% (cost) vs 5-6% (revenue); Large centers benefit from 8-12 months rent-free periods and lower common area % (16% vs 22-25%).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Focus on fit-out capital for high-pre-lease assets; No heavy land acquisition; Reinvesting operating cash flows into rapid Tier-2 expansion.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: DevX's next phase of growth targets expanding operational portfolio from approximately 8.3 Lacs Sq. Ft. to 12 Lacs Sq. Ft. by FY 2027-28, funded via a diversified capital strategy including Non-Convertible Debentures of `100 Crores (indicative coupon 11.75%, listed on BSE Debt Segment) and a preferential issue. Ft. contract adding ~8,500 seats, expected to generate approximately `120 Crores in annual revenue upon stabilisation, supported by a planned investment of `100 Crores over four years. DevX Capital One, Ahmedabad — 3.15 Lacs Sq. Ft. now operational, achieved nearly 95% pre-leasing before commencement, contributing `2.65-2.75 Crores monthly. DevX Million Minds, Ahmedabad — 84,000 Sq. Ft. operational. DevX LakeShore & DevX Featherlite at Outer Ring Road, Bengaluru (Prestige) — 1.1 Lacs Sq. Ft., operational from August 2026, establishing a presence in a premier Bengaluru commercial corridor. Pune expansion — 42,000 Sq. Ft. followed by 2,04,000 Sq. Ft. scheduled for January 2027. DevX 102, Ahmedabad Development Management — 5 Lacs Sq. Ft. targeted to go live in Q4 FY 2026-27, demonstrating scalability of the Development Management model. The company also operates a Development Management model in Ahmedabad's Ambli-Bopal corridor, with approximately 8.60 Lacs Sq. Ft. contracted, generating development management fees of `300-500 per Sq. Ft. in addition to recurring managed-workspace revenues.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident, strategic pivot emphasized, focused on 'virtual entry barriers' in Tier-2, proud of asset-light innovation.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- customer lock-in: long-tenure managed-office contracts with 5-9 year lease terms and 3.5-5 year lock-ins — evidence: zero net churn and 99.7% seat-retention rate in FY 2025-26
- scale: largest managed workspace operator in India's Tier II markets by operational flex stock — evidence: 28 operational centres across 12 cities with 13,604+ seating capacity
- cost position: asset-light straight-lease model bearing only fit-out costs while retaining full revenue upside — evidence: debt-to-equity improved to 0.78x in FY 2025-26 from 2.39x in FY 2024-25 following IPO proceeds
- integration: in-house design-and-build capability removes the largest source of delay in client expansion — evidence: bespoke workspace delivered within 75-90 days via subsidiary Neddle and Thread Designs LLP

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution risk on massive 8 lakh sq. ft. delivery; Concentration in Gujarat/Rajasthan; Potential slowdown in GCC hiring; Competition from institutional players entering Tier-2.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 8 lakh sq. ft. deal is a 'Development Management' contract where DevX acts as the operator/consultant for non-institutional landowners, effectively institutionalizing fragmented Tier-2 supply without balance sheet burden.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Corridor-led, Tier-II focused expansion strategy prioritising enterprise demand over asset ownership
- Asset-light Development Management model: partnering with landowners to create purpose-built, institutional-grade supply based on confirmed enterprise demand rather than leasing ready-made space
- Enterprise-first business design targeting long-term workspace requirements over short-duration coworking demand
- Direct-first client sourcing (reducing reliance on channel partners) to lower acquisition costs and strengthen enterprise engagement
- Integrated platform combining development management, workplace operations and technology (DevX Terra) on a single platform

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for cost-arbitrage and scalable Grade-A infrastructure outside saturated metros | Global Capability Centers (GCCs) | beneficiary | High | DevX provides end-to-end solution (real estate + hiring + tech) in Tier-2 cities where GCCs are migrating for 20-35% cost savings. |
| Fragmented, non-institutional land ownership in Tier-2 cities lacking enterprise-grade assets | Tier-2 Landowners | beneficiary | Med | DevX partners with them to develop Grade-A assets and manages leasing, unlocking value from idle land. |
| High rental costs and saturation in Tier-1 markets | Traditional Tier-1 Co-working Operators | loser | Med | DevX's aggressive Tier-2 focus and asset-light model create a 'virtual entry barrier' making it hard for metro-centric players to compete on cost/scale in emerging cities. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [AI Launchpad] The company is developing "a technology-led real estate ecosystem through the AI Infrastructure Launchpad, which invites AI and PropTech innovators to develop solutions aimed at improving operational efficiency, automating processes, enhancing customer experience and enabling data-driven decision-making".
- [Tokenisation] "Tokenization process has been started, law firm and related consultants on boarded and entity incorporation started"; the Chairman adds that "Recent building tokenisation initiatives and access to global capital are expected to support expansion plans in this area".
- [Investment - Eezily] DevX is "leveraging its investment in Eezily to gain access to broker networks, real estate market intelligence and demand insights, creating synergies between AI, data and its operating platform".
- [Partnership] "The partnership with a leading pan-India media organisation will also provide access to a wider innovation network and help identify scalable technology solutions." (the counterparty is not named in the deck)
- [OpCo-PropCo] The company "Commenced operations as the lessee of the JUPL/AEPL property and will continue to manage the office space under the OpCo-PropCo model", which "Separates operational management from property ownership, enabling scalable and efficient operations".

themes.title: Flexible workspace, PropTech & commercial real-estate services
themes.need: The GCC build-out and hybrid-work shift drive managed/flexible office demand, and Q1FY27 showed flex becoming the marginal buyer of Indian office space. SMARTWORKS grew revenue 44% to INR 546cr with normalized EBITDA INR 107cr (+74%) at a 19.6% margin, lifted GCC clients from 15% to 21% of revenue in a single quarter, and reported India's highest-ever quarterly leasing at 24.6 mn sq ft with 27% of it through flex, up from 19% a year ago. PropTech consolidation started in the same quarter: AURUM announced the acquisition of Housing.com (~24% of India's online-portal share, 58mn monthly visits) at ~1.5x revenue against listed comparables at 4.5-10x, with Housing currently burning ~INR 200cr a year and committed to break even in four to six quarters. AWFIS/EFCIL/INDIQUBE/DEVX/WEWORK add managed workspace; NIRLON on office REIT-proxy assets.
themes.driver: GCC seat-count additions and flex share of net leasing; AURUM's four-to-six-quarter Housing.com breakeven clock; enterprise managed-office wins.
